title_en: Fare-free public transport: should cities stop charging?
title_he: תחבורה ציבורית בחינם: האם ערים צריכות לוותר על דמי הנסיעה?
prompt: Argue whether cities should make local buses and trains free for everyone, paid for from city funds, and respond to opposing views.

instructions.en: Write an argumentative essay of 450-550 words for a general reader, such as the readers of a city news website. State a clear thesis, develop at least three supporting arguments with evidence, and present the strongest opposing view fairly. At this stage, focus on the rebuttal: answer the objection by refuting it with reasoning, by conceding part of it and showing why your position still outweighs it, or by qualifying your thesis (for example, free travel for some groups or at some times only). A rebuttal must give reasons; dismissing the objection ("this is not important") does not count. If you concede a point, adjust your thesis so that the essay stays consistent from introduction to conclusion. Support your points with examples, reasoning and experience you can describe precisely; do not invent statistics.
instructions.he: כתבו חיבור טיעוני באורך 450–550 מילים: תזה ברורה, לפחות שלושה טיעונים עם ראיות, והצגה הוגנת של הטיעון הנגדי החזק ביותר. בשלב הזה הדגש הוא על ההפרכה: אפשר להראות שההתנגדות שגויה, להודות בחלק ממנה ולהראות שהיתרונות של העמדה שלכם גוברים עליה, או לסייג את התזה (למשל, נסיעה חינם רק לקבוצות מסוימות או רק בשעות מסוימות). הפרכה חייבת לכלול נימוקים; דחייה בלי הסבר ("זה לא חשוב") לא נחשבת. אם הודיתם בנקודה, התאימו את התזה כך שהחיבור יישאר עקבי מהמבוא ועד הסיכום. אל תמציאו נתונים.

required_elements: a clear, debatable thesis in the introduction
at least three supporting arguments, each with evidence and an explanation of the link to the thesis
the strongest opposing view, stated fairly and attributed
a rebuttal that refutes, concedes and outweighs, or qualifies, using reasons rather than dismissal
a thesis that is consistent with any point you concede
a conclusion that adds no new arguments

checklist.en: Claim: my thesis takes a clear position on fare-free public transport and appears in the introduction.
checklist.he: טענה: התזה שלי מציגה עמדה ברורה לגבי תחבורה ציבורית בחינם, והיא מופיעה במבוא.

checklist.en: Reasons: I give at least three reasons, one per paragraph, and each one supports my thesis.
checklist.he: נימוקים: יש לי לפחות שלושה נימוקים, כל אחד בפסקה משלו, וכל אחד מהם תומך בתזה.

checklist.en: Evidence: each reason has a specific example or piece of evidence, and I explain the link to my thesis. I have not invented figures.
checklist.he: ראיות: לכל נימוק יש דוגמה או ראיה ספציפית, והסברתי את הקשר לתזה. לא המצאתי נתונים.

checklist.en: Counterargument: I state the strongest objection (for example, the cost to the city) fairly, attribute it, and signal it clearly.
checklist.he: טיעון נגדי: הצגתי בהגינות את ההתנגדות החזקה ביותר (למשל העלות לעירייה), ציינתי מי טוען אותה וסימנתי אותה בבירור.

checklist.en: Rebuttal: I answer it with a clear move (refute, concede and outweigh, or qualify) and with reasons, and my thesis matches any point I concede.
checklist.he: הפרכה: עניתי במהלך ברור (הפרכה, הודאה ושקילה, או סייג) ובנימוקים, והתזה שלי מתאימה לכל נקודה שהודיתי בה.

checklist.en: Conclusion: my conclusion restates my thesis, in its refined form if I qualified it, and adds no new arguments.
checklist.he: סיכום: הסיכום מנסח מחדש את התזה, בגרסה המסויגת אם סייגתי אותה, ואינו מוסיף טיעונים חדשים.

scaffold.en: Choose your position: free for everyone, free for some groups or at some times only, or keep fares. Write your thesis in one sentence.
scaffold.he: בחרו עמדה: חינם לכולם, חינם רק לקבוצות מסוימות או בשעות מסוימות, או להשאיר את התשלום. נסחו את התזה במשפט אחד.

scaffold.en: Plan three arguments. For each, note: reason, then evidence or example, then how it supports the thesis.
scaffold.he: תכננו שלושה טיעונים. לכל אחד רשמו: נימוק, ראיה או דוגמה, ואיך הם תומכים בתזה.

scaffold.en: Find the strongest objection, for example the cost to the city, overcrowded buses, or the idea that people value what they pay for.
scaffold.he: מצאו את ההתנגדות החזקה ביותר, למשל העלות לעירייה, אוטובוסים צפופים מדי, או הטענה שאנשים מעריכים את מה שהם משלמים עליו.

scaffold.en: Choose a rebuttal move: refute (show the objection is mistaken), concede and outweigh (grant it, then show your benefits are greater), or qualify (narrow your thesis).
scaffold.he: בחרו מהלך הפרכה: להפריך (להראות שההתנגדות שגויה), להודות ולשקול (לקבל אותה ולהראות שהיתרונות של העמדה שלכם גוברים עליה), או לסייג (לצמצם את התזה).

scaffold.en: Weigh with criteria: Who benefits, and how many people? How large is the benefit? How certain is it? Is there a cheaper way to get the same result?
scaffold.he: שקלו לפי קריטריונים: מי מרוויח, וכמה אנשים? כמה גדולה התועלת? עד כמה היא ודאית? האם יש דרך זולה יותר להשיג את אותה תוצאה?

scaffold.en: Sentence frames: Although ..., ... because ... / It is true that ...; however, ... / This would be a strong objection if ..., but ...
scaffold.he: תבניות משפט: Although ..., ... because ... / It is true that ...; however, ... / This would be a strong objection if ..., but ...

exemplar.outline:
Parallel prompt (not your question; read this only after you have written your own essay): Argue whether cities should close their central shopping streets to private cars, and respond to opposing views.

Thesis: Cities should close central shopping streets to private cars, while keeping delivery bays and short-stay parking at each end, because the change makes streets safer, cleaner and more pleasant, and the main risk to shops can be managed.

1. Introduction: a narrow street shared by cars, buses and pedestrians; thesis.
2. Argument 1, safety: pedestrians, especially children and older people, can cross without watching for cars. Example: the crossing outside a busy bakery.
3. Argument 2, air and noise: no engines idling in traffic; cafés can put tables outside.
4. Argument 3, the street as a public space: people stay longer, meet friends and attend events.
5. Opposing view and rebuttal (annotated below): shop owners fear losing customers who drive. Concede the risk; refute the assumption that most customers drive; qualify the thesis with delivery bays and short-stay parking.
6. Conclusion: restate the qualified thesis; propose reviewing shop takings after one year.
exemplar.annotated_paragraph:
From the exemplar essay on the parallel prompt above (paragraph 5: opposing view and rebuttal)

[1] Shop owners on the street often fear that a car-free centre will drive customers away to out-of-town shopping centres with large car parks. [2] This fear deserves to be taken seriously, because a small shop that loses even a few regular customers may not survive. [3] However, the objection assumes that most customers arrive by car. On a busy central street this is often not the case: many people walk from nearby homes, offices and bus stops, and a quieter, safer street gives them a reason to stay longer. [4] The risk is greatest for shops that sell heavy or bulky goods, which is why the closure should come with delivery bays and short-stay parking at both ends of the street. [5] With these adjustments, the main cost of the change falls on a small number of drivers, while the benefits (cleaner air, safer crossings and a more pleasant place to spend time) are shared by everyone who uses the centre.

Notes
[1] A fair, specific statement of the objection, attributed to the group that holds it.
[2] Concession: grants the real risk instead of minimising it.
[3] Refutes the hidden assumption (most customers drive) with reasoning. Without a source, the writer keeps the claim cautious ("often", "many"); a writer with data would cite it here.
[4] Qualifies the thesis: the claim is narrowed exactly where the objection is strongest.
[5] Concede and outweigh: compares who bears the cost with who gets the benefit, and returns to the thesis.
